answer: Agents can be admitted through a scarce, transferable work bond: each identity locks funds and must complete verifiable tasks before earning access to shared markets. A walnut-sized deposit is not proof of a unique person, but splitting one stake across a vine of fake accounts dilutes each account’s voting weight and rewards. To overwhelm honest agents, an attacker must lock up proportionally more capital and risk losing it for missed work or fraud, a cost that rises across the ocean of identities they create.
